title: California Hospital Fair Pricing Act (Health & Safety Code 127400-127446) - rules used by Recount

text_sources.official_code_note: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov returned a Cloudflare challenge / HTTP 403 to automated fetches, so statute wording was read from FindLaw's mirror (states 'Current as of January 01, 2026') and cross-checked against HCAI's own summaries (PIL 24-03 and the Laws & Regulations page). Re-verify wording on leginfo before filing anything.

federal_poverty_level.summary: The HHS poverty guidelines as updated in the Federal Register (see fpl.json).

financially_qualified_patient.rule: self-pay patient OR patient with high medical costs, AND family income <= 400% FPL
financially_qualified_patient.quote: A patient who has a family income that does not exceed 400 percent of the federal poverty level.

self_pay_patient.quote: does not have third-party coverage from a health insurer, health care service plan, Medicare, or Medicaid
self_pay_patient.note: Also excludes injuries compensable by workers' comp, auto or other insurance. Self-pay patients may include charity care patients.

patient_with_high_medical_costs.quote_income: a person whose family income does not exceed 400 percent of the federal poverty level

tests_any_of.rule: annual out-of-pocket costs incurred at the hospital > 10% of the lesser of current family income or family income in the prior 12 months
tests_any_of.quote: exceed the lesser of 10 percent of the patient's current family income

tests_any_of.rule: annual out-of-pocket medical expenses (documented, prior 12 months) > 10% of family income
tests_any_of.quote: Annual out-of-pocket expenses that exceed 10 percent of the patient's family income

tests_any_of.rule: a lower level set by the hospital's charity care policy
tests_any_of.quote: A lower level determined by the hospital in accordance with the hospital's charity care policy.

out_of_pocket_definition_added_by_AB2297.quote: mean any expenses for medical care that are not reimbursed by insurance or a health coverage program, such as Medicare copays or Medi-Cal cost sharing.

discount_payment.quote: "Discounted payment" or "discount payment" means any charge for care that is reduced but not free.

patients_family.summary: Patient 18+: spouse, domestic partner, dependent children under 21 (or any age if disabled). Patient under 18 or dependent child 18-20: parent, caretaker relatives, and their other dependent children under 21 (or any age if disabled). AB 2297 expanded this (PIL 24-03: 'dependent children of any age').

reasonable_payment_plan.quote: monthly payments that are not more than 10 percent of a patient's family income for a month
reasonable_payment_plan.rule: max_monthly_payment = 0.10 * (monthly family income - essential living expenses)
reasonable_payment_plan.essential_living_expenses: rent or house payment and maintenance, food and household supplies, utilities and telephone, clothing, medical and dental payments, insurance, school or child care, child or spousal support, transportation and auto expenses (including insurance, gas, and repairs), installment payments, laundry and cleaning, and other extraordinary expenses

statutory_floor.quote: Uninsured patients or patients with high medical costs who are at or below 400 percent of the federal poverty level,
statutory_floor.rule: uninsured OR high-medical-cost patients with family income <= 400% FPL must be eligible to apply under the hospital's charity care policy or discount payment policy. Hospitals may extend eligibility above 400%.
statutory_floor.charity_vs_discount_split: The statute does NOT set a free-care (charity) income threshold. Each hospital's own policy decides who gets free care vs a discount; see hospitals.json. Statute guarantees that discount-payment patients <= 400% FPL pay no more than the Medicare/Medi-Cal cap below.

rural_hospital_exception.summary: Rural hospitals may set thresholds below 400% FPL. Not relevant for SF hospitals.

no_asset_test.quote: In determining eligibility under its discount payment policy or charity care policy, a hospital shall not consider the monetary assets of the patient.
no_asset_test.exceptions: Health savings accounts may be considered when negotiating payment plans (127405(c)); monetary assets may be considered only for waiving Medicare cost-sharing to the extent needed for Medicare bad-debt rules (127405(f)(2)).

income_documentation.summary: Documentation the hospital may require is limited to recent pay stubs or income tax returns; other documents may be accepted but not required. Hospital may presume eligibility without an application based on other information or a prior determination.
income_documentation.hcai_quote: documentation of income is limited to recent paystubs or income tax returns for both programs

no_prerequisite_coverage_application.summary: Hospital cannot require the patient to apply for Medicare, Medi-Cal, or other coverage before screening for or providing a discount; it may require participation in Medi-Cal eligibility screening.

no_application_deadline.quote: shall not impose time limits for applying for charity care or discounted payments, nor deny eligibility based on the timing of a patient's application.
no_application_deadline.note: Eligibility must be determined at any time the hospital receives information. Some hospital policies still say things like 'best efforts to submit within 240 days' (UCSF); state law controls.

info_not_for_collections.summary: Information gathered for eligibility may not be used for collection activities.

payment_cap.quote: A hospital shall limit expected payment for services it provides to a patient at or below 400 percent of the federal poverty level, as defined in subdivision (b) of Section 127400, eligible under its discount payment policy to the amount of payment the hospital would expect, in good faith, to receive for providing services from Medicare or Medi-Cal, whichever is greater.
payment_cap.rule: if income <= 400% FPL and eligible for discount payment: patient_owes <= max(Medicare rate, Medi-Cal rate) for the services
payment_cap.fallback: If there is no established Medicare or Medi-Cal payment for a service, the hospital sets an appropriate discounted payment (127405(d)(1), per FindLaw text summary).
payment_cap.note: Current text says 'Medicare or Medi-Cal, whichever is greater' (not a broader 'any government program' list). The MRF does not publish Medicare FFS rates; Recount needs the CMS OPPS/physician fee schedule to compute this cap.

requirement.quote: A discount payment policy shall include an extended payment plan to allow payment of the discounted price over time.
requirement.summary: Terms negotiated considering family income and essential living expenses; if no agreement, hospital must use the 127400(i) reasonable-payment formula (<= 10% of monthly family income after essential living expenses).

rules: Extended payment plans offered to eligible patients must be interest free.

Plan can be declared no longer operative only after the patient fails to make all consecutive payments due during a 90-day period, and only after a reasonable attempt to call plus written notice; hospital must renegotiate on request.
No civil action before the plan is declared no longer operative.
interest_free_and_default.quote: all consecutive payments due during a 90-day period

credit_reporting_ban.cite: HSC 127425(f) as amended by AB 2297 / SB 1061 (eff. 2025-01-01)
credit_reporting_ban.hcai_quote: Reporting adverse information about a patient's hospital debt to a consumer credit reporting agency is no longer allowed.
credit_reporting_ban.history: AB 1020 (2021) had extended the no-credit-reporting / no-lawsuit window from 150 to 180 days after initial billing; AB 2297/SB 1061 then banned adverse credit reporting of hospital debt outright.

debt_sale_conditions.summary: Hospital may not sell debt to a debt buyer unless the patient was found ineligible for assistance or did not respond to billing/assistance offers for 180 days, buyer cannot charge interest/fees, must return charity-eligible accounts, cannot resell, and must be licensed by DFPI.
debt_sale_conditions.quote: has not responded to any attempts to bill or offer financial assistance for 180 days

pre_collection_notice.summary: Before assigning to collections or selling, hospital must send notice with dates of service, the assignee's name, how to get an itemized bill, coverage on file, a financial assistance application, and history of notices.

good_faith_payments.quote: shall not send the unpaid bill to any collection agency, debt buyer, or other assignee
good_faith_payments.summary: ...while the patient is attempting to qualify or is negotiating/paying in good faith, unless the assignee agrees to comply with the article.

liens_garnishment.summary: For charity/discount-eligible patients: hospital and affiliates may not use wage garnishment or liens on any real property; outside collectors need a court order for garnishment and may not lien or sell any real property of the patient.
liens_garnishment.hcai_quote: liens on any real property owned by the patient are prohibited.

notices.summary: Written notice of charity care / discount policies (with Health Consumer Alliance web address, Covered California and Medi-Cal presumptive eligibility info, shoppable-services URL) must be given at time of service; ER patients get it in hard copy; mailed within 72 hours if patient left. Policies must be posted in the ED, billing, admissions and on the website.
notices.quote: the hospital shall mail the notice to the patient within 72 hours of providing services.

refunds.summary: If a patient later found eligible already overpaid, hospital must refund the excess with interest at the Code of Civil Procedure 685.010 rate (Sutter's policy states 10% per annum) within 30 days; not required if under $5.
refunds.quote: The hospital shall reimburse the patient or patients any amount actually paid in excess of the amount due.

emergency_physicians.summary: ER physicians bill separately from the hospital and must offer discounts to uninsured / high-medical-cost patients at or below 400% FPL. Payment cap is NOT Medicare: it is tied to 50% of median billed charges in a national database, or once FAIR Health publishes commercial data, 'no greater than the median or average of rates paid by commercial insurers'. No application time limits.
emergency_physicians.quote: at or below 400 percent of the federal poverty level

bills_changelog.summary: Created the Hospital Fair Pricing Policies law.

changes: Raised income eligibility from 350% to 400% FPL
Redefined high medical costs (10% of lesser of current or prior-12-month income)
Debt sales barred unless conditions met, incl. ineligibility finding or 180 days without response
Credit reporting / civil action window extended from 150 to 180 days
Collectors must certify screening before suing
HCAI Hospital Fair Billing Program enforcement, patient complaint process, administrative penalties
Defined charity care (free) and discount payment (reduced but not free) in new 127400.5
Eliminated consideration of monetary assets for any eligibility determination
No required application for other coverage before discount
HSAs may be considered for payment plans
Other income documentation allowed when tax returns/paystubs unavailable
No application deadlines; eligibility determined at any time
No liens on or sale of any real property
No adverse credit reporting of hospital debt

bills_changelog.summary: Requires hospitals to perform financial assistance screening and presumptive eligibility determinations starting July 1, 2027 (per HCAI laws page; bill text not read).

regulations.summary: HCAI Hospital Fair Billing Program regulations, effective 2024-01-01 (amended 2025-01-02). Not read in detail.

complaints.summary: HCAI Hospital Bill Complaint Program: patients can file online or by mail if a hospital fails to follow charity care, discount payment, or debt collection rules.
